questions.title: What can you do when your ball is in a penalty area (like a pond or creek)?
questions.question: Your ball is in a penalty area, like a puddle or next to some water. What can you do next?

choices.text: Play the ball from where it is in the penalty area, and keep going without any extra shots added.
Drop your ball outside the penalty area and add one shot to your score.
Drop a second ball anywhere you want inside the penalty area, without adding any shots.
You must go back and hit from where you first played your shot.

questions.explanation: You can play your ball as it is in the penalty area with no extra shots, or you can take your ball out and drop it outside, but you must add one shot to your score.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A place on the golf course with water or red or yellow stakes, like a pond or stream. If your ball ends up here, there are special rules.
Letting your ball go from knee height so it lands on the ground to play your next shot.

questions.teachingTip: Show kids the difference between a penalty area and the rest of the course. Let them practise dropping a ball to understand how relief outside the penalty area works.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids might think you always have to take a penalty when your ball is in a penalty area, even if you want to play it as it lies.
They might also believe you can drop the ball anywhere you like in the penalty area without penalty, which is not true.

questions.title: Options for playing from a penalty area
questions.question: After your ball is found in a penalty area, what choices do you have about playing your next shot?

choices.text: Play the ball as it lies inside the penalty area, with no extra penalty.
Take a drop outside the penalty area, with a one-stroke penalty.
Drop a second ball anywhere in the penalty area, without penalty.
You must return to the teeing area and replay the shot.

questions.explanation: You may play the ball as it lies in the penalty area (with no extra penalty) or take penalty area relief by dropping outside the penalty area for one penalty stroke.
